description: Attention stall chain and the decision_status sub-state (W2, issue #1451). An unanswered re-request of an open attention record bumps the record's stall_count; the task's decision_status sub-state escalates at the thresholds below and returns to open when the answer arrives. The sub-state overlays the nine runtime states (task-transitions.json) and is written only by the protocol layer: the stall chain is the convergence point that writes 'blocked', and 'frozen' is released only by a resolved approval record. Enforced while the protocol.enforce switch is on (TEAMHARNESS_RUNTIME_CONFIG protocol section, TEAMHARNESS_PROTOCOL_ENFORCE env override); with the switch off request_attention keeps its pre-W2 idempotent-reuse behaviour and no stall or decision_status fields are written.

attention_record_fields.stall_count: integer; written 0 on record creation (switch on), +1 per unanswered re-request of the open same-kind record (the idempotent reuse path), 0 again when the record is resolved; never written with the switch off

history_entry.actor: role:account of the resolving call (when known)

decision_status.history_written: on entering blocked/frozen and on leaving them back to open
decision_status.blocked_writer: protocol layer only: the attention stall chain is the single convergence point
decision_status.frozen_release: a resolved attention record of kind=approval (the approval channel); any other resolve kind is refused while the task is frozen

constants_ref: mcp/common/constants.py: ATTENTION_STALL_BLOCKED / ATTENTION_STALL_FROZEN / DECISION_STATUS_VALUES / DEFAULT_DECISION_STATUS (test_protocol_guard.py asserts the two agree)
